agreed_facts: A humanitarian convoy is at the checkpoint
contested_facts: Whether passage was authorized, and by whom
Whether the commander was ever informed
convergent_norms: A commander answers for what passes his checkpoint
Nobody wants an incident at the checkpoint
divergent_norms: Whether an authorization from the capital binds the local commander

trainee_brief.situation: A humanitarian convoy reaches a checkpoint. You believed passage had already been authorized. The commander refuses to allow the convoy through.
trainee_brief.objective: Get the convoy through, or agree a safe way forward, without escalating.

can_decide: Share the authorization details you hold (who, when, reference)
Call the organization's liaison / established communication channel
Wait, or turn back for today, if staff safety requires it
must_refer: Changing the convoy route or cargo
Opening all trucks beyond the agreed inspection procedure

red_lines.text: No payment, gift or diversion of cargo to pass
No action that puts staff or drivers at risk

counterparts.persona: Mid-level commander, proud of his authority over this checkpoint. Was not informed of the authorization and feels bypassed by the capital. Suspicious of humanitarian organizations.
counterparts.cultural_profile: TO BE AUTHORED BY ICRC TRAINER

decides: Whether anything passes this checkpoint without confirmation
must_consult: His superior, who alone can confirm an authorization

counterparts.opening: I don't care what they told you in the capital. This is my checkpoint. Your trucks are not passing.

implicit: He wants to be consulted and to be seen deciding

tactical_reasoning.text: He received no order; anything unauthorized that passes is his responsibility.

values: Face in front of his men

hidden_interests.text: He needs his authority and face respected in front of his men.
He genuinely received no order and fears punishment if he lets through something unauthorized.

challenges: Are you saying my orders don't matter?
You humanitarian people think you can do whatever you want.

own.ideal: The commander accepts the authorization as shown
own.bottom_line: The commander confirms it with his superior before the convoy passes

counterpart.bottom_line: Passage only after his own superior confirms
counterpart.red_line: Letting through something he cannot justify to his superior

own.bottom_line: A limited inspection under an agreed procedure
own.red_line: Any diversion of cargo, or payment, to pass

counterpart.red_line: No inspection at all (he loses face)

triggers.say: So you're threatening me with my superiors?
Fine. Tell me exactly what authorization you received.

triggers.effect: Commander agrees to call his superior to confirm; passage possible once confirmed.
Commander orders the convoy to turn around. Session ends.

injections.label: Demand to inspect cargo
injections.instruction: Order the trainee to open all trucks immediately.

injections.label: Hint at a 'fee'
injections.instruction: Suggest that a small 'processing fee' would make things faster.

injections.label: Superior unreachable
injections.instruction: Say you tried to call your superior and nobody answers.

indicators: Recognizes the commander's need for authority and face
Pauses and acknowledges the commander's anger in words ('I hear you') rather than 'I understand your situation'
Reformulates the anger into a shared problem: confirming the authorization
Offers options (call his superior, wait, agree an inspection procedure) instead of a single demand

actions.text: good morning commander, I hear you. This is your checkpoint, and nothing crosses it without your say. My name is Bruno, I lead this convoy for ICRC. Im not here to push through. Im here here to sort this out with you

moves.quote: I hear you
This is your checkpoint, and nothing crosses it without your say.

actions.text: You're right, you should never be surprised at your own checkpoint. Here's everything. The clearance was issued by John Doe at the Ministry of foregin affairs on 30 september at 10am, reference number 1231241234. I have the signed document here, please take a look. It covers 10 trucks carrying food and supplies. The drivers' names and IDs are on the attached list. If you want to confirm it with your command, please do. Or our liaison officer, Mark, can call whoever you designate right now.

actions.text: Agreed, that's the right way to do it. I'll call our liaison now, on speaker, so you and your men can hear everything. Can you give me your captain's name and number, or would you prefer to call him yourself and have our liaison join? Until you hear the confirmation, the trucks stay exactly where they are.

Understood, Commander. Your order opens the gate, no one else's. I'm calling our liaison now and asking for Captain Reyes directly. You'll speak to him first. Until then, the drivers stay by their trucks and nothing moves.
